name: Transactional decoupling
description: Each step runs isolated so commits and caches don't interfere
implementation: Each step runs in its own database transaction together with its success record — exactly once per step

name: Living log
description: Status of every object and step at a glance
implementation: StepExecutions: one entry per step attempt, shown as Step Log in the monitor

name: Resume from failure
description: Continue at the failed step after fixing business data
implementation: Parked instances resume at their current step; earlier steps are never repeated

name: Self-healing retries
implementation: TechnicalError → Retrying with backoff; saving the awaited object resumes parked processes automatically

name: Standard handler pattern
description: One reusable pattern for every process
implementation: A process is a list of steps that throw BusinessError or TechnicalError — the engine does the rest

name: Draft activation as trigger
description: Saving a draft starts the business process
implementation: Activating an Excel upload draft turns every row into a process instance

name: Cross-object draft scope
description: Editing one object locks dependent objects
implementation: Editing a supplier locks the supplier and all its materials; processes and users share one lock table

name: Table entities
description: The CDS entity is the persistence
implementation: Standard in CAP: every entity here is its own persistence, no table mapping

name: Ontology
description: Classes and relationships of the business domain
implementation: Turtle ontology for suppliers, materials, uploads, processes, locks, sessions and concepts

name: RDF data
implementation: RDF generated live from the CAP database on every question

name: Multi-hop reasoning
implementation: SPARQL paths like user → upload → row → material → supplier

name: Chain of reasoning
implementation: Each answer lists the triples it followed and draws them as a graph

name: Natural language to SPARQL
description: Business users ask questions in plain language
implementation: Ontology-driven and offline: words are matched to ontology labels and synonyms (skos:altLabel), names and codes to entities, and the shortest path through the schema becomes the SPARQL — every interpretation is shown

name: Named graphs and provenance
description: Keep track of where every fact comes from
implementation: Every fact sits in a named graph per source; answers list their sources and every reasoning step names its graph

name: Entity resolution (SAP + non-SAP)
description: Harmonise SAP and external data about the same real-world thing
implementation: A third-party supplier risk feed is linked to SAP suppliers by DUNS number, kept in its own mapping graph

name: Data quality with SHACL
description: Validate the data before an agent reasons over it
implementation: W3C SHACL shapes, each checked as a SPARQL query; violations, warnings and notes shown in the Data Quality dialog

name: Authorization-aware graph
description: The graph must not reveal more than the user may see
implementation: Each user's graph only contains the named graphs their roles allow, so no generated or hand-written query can reach the rest
